summary: Proposes an ASCII text file of hostnames, related to RFCs 606, 608, 623 and 625.

eli5.summary: A plain text file lists the names of the network's computers so any program can read it.

questions: how did the nic manage computer names
subtitle: The official list of ARPANET computers and their addresses.

tldr.problem: The ARPANET needed a single, consistent list of computer names and addresses that all sites could reference.
tldr.mechanism: The Network Information Center maintains an ASCII text file called HOSTS.TXT with each computer's name, address and status, available via FTP at a known location.
tldr.outcome: Every ARPANET site can fetch the latest hostnames file and stay synchronized, enabling reliable name-to-address lookups across the network.

today: RFC 627 describes the first generation of centralized hostname distribution on the ARPANET, which evolved into the Domain Name System (DNS).

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: RFC 627 announces that the official ARPANET hostnames file is now available online at OFFICE-1 (address 43 decimal) with the filename <NETINFO>HOSTS.TXT. The file is maintained by the Network Information Center and contains the hostname, address and status for each computer on the network. Sites are encouraged to use these official hostnames in their monitoring systems rather than maintaining private lists.
sections.eli5: There is now one official list of all the network computers and where to find it, and everyone should use that instead of making their own lists.

sections.title: File Contents and Updates
sections.content: The HOSTS.TXT file is plain ASCII text listing each computer name, its numeric address and its current status. The NIC plans to add more attributes in the future. The file is updated on a weekly basis, and each site is responsible for using FTP to regularly download the latest copy. Sites that wish to maintain secondary copies of the database are encouraged to register with the NIC.
sections.eli5: The file is a simple text list that gets updated every week, and any computer can copy it to stay up to date.

sections.title: Hostnames and Nicknames
sections.content: Each computer gets one official hostname, chosen carefully to minimize future changes. Sites may register an optional nickname for their computer if desired. The RFC asks sites to choose official hostnames thoughtfully to keep the database stable. All requests for additions, changes or corrections should be directed to the Network Information Center contact at Stanford Research Institute.
sections.eli5: Every computer gets one official name that won't change much, and can have a nickname too. Picking good names keeps the list clean.

references.text: Kudlick, M. and J. Feinler, "ASCII Text File of Hostnames", RFC 627, March 1974.
